<div class="hero-summary">
  <p>A capstone begins with an interest and has to end, by January, with a plan
  somebody could actually execute. This course builds that plan in the order the
  work really happens: form a question, work out what evidence would answer it,
  and only then go looking for data — because the design is what tells you which
  data you need, and teams who find data first end up rationalizing a question
  around whatever they found. The conceptual core is the causal language
  economists use — counterfactuals, graphs, the standard threats, and the
  designs that get around them — taught on examples from industry and the news
  before anyone opens a dataset. The back half is judgment about data: knowing
  what to ask of a dataset, driving an AI assistant to answer it, checking
  whether the answer is credible, and seeing what a figure shows and hides. It
  is not a coding course — no prior econometrics or programming is assumed, and
  none is taught.</p>
</div>
